cases.reason: Flag pending-clause §2002:14.5.12.1.2 attacked. The answer says the 2023 additions to the fatal order 'are 2023 constructs or come before the propagation step'; SORT and MERGE are 2002 statements, and 2023's item 2 ('If the executed statement is a MERGE or SORT statement, then the rules for those statements apply') PRE-EMPTS propagation. 2002's fatal order has no such item: with checking enabled, no applicable USE and PROPAGATE ON, item 3 propagates the condition. So the 2002 rule's scope includes a fatal condition raised by a SORT (or MERGE) in an element under PROPAGATE ON, which the 2023 twin's evidence does not reach (2023 diverts it), and the 2002 SORT rules address only a NON-FATAL condition of the USING file's implicit OPEN (§2002:14.8.36.3 GR11a). Probe prop-sort.cob at --std 2002: SSUB under >>PROPAGATE ON with >>TURN EC-I-O CHECKING ON does SORT ... USING a missing file: prints 'SSUB CONTINUED FS=35' then 'MAIN AFTER' (no propagation; the caller's USE EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR declarative is never entered). Controls: prop-open.cob (plain OPEN INPUT of the same file) propagates at 2002 ('MAIN CAUGHT EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR', then abnormal termination); prop-sort-own.cob shows the SORT's condition IS raised and enabled (SSUB's own declarative prints EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR). The compiler applies 2023's §14.6.13.1.3 2) (EcEmitter __verbRule) at every edition. Lead beyond this row: prop-sort-own continues after the declarative completes normally at 2002, where §2002:14.5.12.1.2 item 2 says the run unit then terminates abnormally.
